In the {G}days gone {D}by, when the {C} world was much {G}younger                                                 
{G}men wondered in {D}spring, born of {C}winter´s  {D}cold {G}knife.                                                            
{G}Wondering at the {D}games of the m{C}oon and the s{G}unlight,                                                
{G}they saw there the {D} Lady and {C}Lord of  {D}all  {G}life.

       Round and around, and around turns the good earth;
       all things must change, as the seasons go by.
       We are the children oft he Lord and the Lady,
       who´s mysteries we know, but we´ll never know why.

In all lands the people where tried tot he good earth,
ploughing and sowing as the seasons go by.
Waiting to reap oft he rich golden harvest,
knowing their joy in the laughs that they shared.

Trough Flanders and Wales and the green land of Ireland,
in the Kingdom of England and Scotland and Spain,
circles grew up all along in the wild coastlines
and worked fort he land with the sun and the rain.

Circles for healing and working the weather.
Circles for knowing the moon and the sun.
Circles for thanking the Lord and the Lady.
Circles for dancing the dance´s never done.
title: Circles
